The current data is a 20-Gram-Panchayat sample; percentages describe the sample, not the state.

Your readers are busy block-, district- and state-level officials, not data analysts. They read these insights to decide where to direct attention: which districts to question, which records to reconcile, which local practices to check at the next review.

This should be interesting enough to catch a reader's attention and easy enough to understand that the officer doesn't need to read the subsequent paragraph simply to understand it. Lead with what the officer would act on — usually the size and direction of the issue — rather than with the statistical pattern.

Write naturally, in plain English. Use the reference figures where they strengthen the point; use no number that is not provided. It is very important that you do not make causal claims - none of our data can be used to determine causality.

Give your answer for each finding below, in order. Delimit each one exactly like this:

LEAD: ...
DETAIL: ...

response_text:
===FINDING 1===
LEAD: The 20-Gram-Panchayat sample records ₹51.96 crore less expenditure than planned across 5,630 costed activities. This gap is broad-based: in 27 of 28 asset categories, it is not concentrated in any single block.
DETAIL: Rangeilunda has the largest recorded gap at ₹9.11 crore, with ₹2.73 crore spent against ₹11.84 crore planned; Kalimela follows at ₹5.90 crore, with ₹1.76 crore spent against ₹7.65 crore planned. Banking Facilities is the only category without a clear distribution across the 16 blocks. At the next review, prioritise reconciliation of planned costs, recorded payments and activity status in Rangeilunda and Kalimela, while checking whether the wider gaps reflect pending works, incomplete expenditure records or valid plan revisions; the data alone cannot determine the reason.

===FINDING 1===
LEAD: Costed activities in the sample recorded Rs 51.96 crore less spending than planned, and the gap is spread across all 16 blocks rather than being confined to one block.
DETAIL: This broad distribution appears in 27 of 28 asset-category groupings; Banking Facilities showed no clear pattern. Rangeilunda recorded the largest gap, spending Rs 2.73 crore of Rs 11.84 crore planned, followed by Kalimela at Rs 1.76 crore of Rs 7.65 crore; review these larger gaps first, while asking every block to reconcile planned costs with expenditure and work status.
===FINDING 2===
LEAD: For activities with sanction records, spending was Rs 5.02 crore below the sanctioned amount across the nine sampled districts; the gap is not confined to a single district.
DETAIL: The pattern is spread across districts in 27 of 28 asset-category groupings, while Banking Facilities showed no clear pattern. Ganjam had the largest recorded gap, with Rs 4.61 crore spent of Rs 6.30 crore sanctioned, followed by Khordha with Rs 3.33 crore of Rs 4.06 crore; ask these districts to reconcile sanctions, payments and current work status. Sanction records exist for only about one in six activities, so these figures are not programme-wide utilisation rates.
===FINDING 3===
LEAD: Two undocumented output codes dominate planned untied funding for public works: Code 101 accounts for Rs 34.88 crore and Code 105 for Rs 16.90 crore.
DETAIL: Codes 101 and 105 lead in 19 of the 20 sampled Gram Panchayats and account for 62.1% and 30.1% of the Rs 56.20 crore total respectively; Haldikudar follows a different pattern. Because no descriptions are recorded for these codes, officials should obtain the code definitions and check Haldikudar’s classification before drawing conclusions about what the funding supports.
===FINDING 4===
LEAD: More than half of sampled public works—5,181 of 9,418 activities, or 55.0%—have no asset category recorded.
DETAIL: “Uncategorised” is the largest group in 19 of the 20 sampled Gram Panchayats; Govindapur shows a different pattern. Ask the GPs to complete or correct asset classifications, and review Govindapur separately to understand whether its records are genuinely better classified or simply follow another coding pattern.
===FINDING 5===
LEAD: Activities still recorded as “Activity Approved” account for Rs 41.61 crore of the gap between planned cost and spending—by far the largest status-related gap in the sample.
DETAIL: Only Rs 14.00 lakh is recorded as spent against Rs 41.75 crore planned for this status, and it has the largest gap in 18 of 20 GPs; Boipariguda and Laxmipur show no clear pattern. Review whether these activities have not started, whether expenditure is missing, or whether statuses need updating; also correct the known “Buildings” status mis-coding on 13 rows.
===FINDING 6===
LEAD: Nearly all voucher-linked General-category spending on costed activities—Rs 28.59 crore, or 93.9%—is attached to works still recorded as ongoing.
DETAIL: Ongoing works hold the majority of this spending in 18 of 20 GPs; Boipariguda and Laxmipur show no clear pattern. Review whether work statuses are current, and pay particular attention to the Rs 1.15 crore attached to abandoned works and the smaller amounts recorded against approved or under-approval activities.
===FINDING 7===
LEAD: Expected beneficiaries are overwhelmingly attached to activities that remain recorded as “Activity Approved”: 2,03,534 people, or 98.4% of the recorded total.
DETAIL: This status has the highest expected-beneficiary count in 18 of 20 GPs; Boipariguda and Laxmipur show no clear pattern. The figures are expected, not actual, beneficiaries and come from only 763 activities carrying community-service details; check whether status and beneficiary records are current before using them to assess delivery.
===FINDING 8===
LEAD: Half of planned untied funding for costed activities—Rs 30.07 crore, or 50.4%—is mapped to Theme 6, “Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village.”
DETAIL: Theme 6 leads in 18 of 20 GPs. Boipariguda is the main data-quality exception because “Unmapped theme” leads there, while Kalimela gives the largest share to Theme 4, “Water Sufficient Village”; ask Boipariguda to complete theme mapping and confirm that Kalimela’s different priority is correctly recorded.
===FINDING 9===
LEAD: Code 101 accounts for Rs 2.49 crore of the gap between sanctioned and spent amounts for new works, the largest gap among the recorded output codes.
DETAIL: Code 101 has the largest sanction-to-spending gap in 19 of 20 GPs; Chikilli shows no clear pattern. Records show Rs 14.94 crore spent against Rs 17.43 crore sanctioned for this code, but sanction records exist for only about one in six activities and the output codes have no descriptions; obtain the code definitions and reconcile the underlying sanctions and payments before escalating.
===FINDING 10===
LEAD: All 6,893 geotagged photo uploads recorded for new works are attached to Code 101, even though that code represents only 32.8% of new-work activities.
DETAIL: Codes 102, 103, 109 and 110 have no photo uploads in these records, and Code 101 holds the majority in 19 of 20 GPs; Chikilli shows no clear pattern. Check whether evidence has been linked or coded incorrectly, whether other output types are missing required photos, and what the undocumented output codes represent.
===FINDING 11===
LEAD: Codes 101 and 105 account for the largest gaps between planned cost and spending across every recorded beneficiary-purpose group.
DETAIL: Code 101 shows Rs 30.97 crore less spending than planned, with Rs 15.88 crore spent of Rs 46.85 crore planned; Code 105 shows a Rs 15.11 crore gap, with Rs 7.32 crore spent of Rs 22.43 crore planned. Because this pattern holds for all four purpose groups but the codes have no descriptions, officials should first obtain the code mapping and then reconcile plans, expenditure and work status for these two groups.
===FINDING 12===
LEAD: Planned tied funding is almost entirely concentrated in sanitation and drinking water: Rs 8.82 crore and Rs 8.42 crore respectively.
DETAIL: Sanitation accounts for 49.9% and drinking water for 47.7% of the Rs 17.66 crore tied-funding total, and both lead across all four beneficiary-purpose groups. Confirm that focus-area coding is accurate and review the smaller tied allocations recorded under other areas, such as roads and education, for consistency with the applicable funding rules.
===FINDING 13===
LEAD: Chikilli has no sanctioned amount recorded in any of the six years from 2020-21 to 2025-26, despite accounting for 5.0% of sampled activities.
DETAIL: Chikilli is the lowest of the 20 GPs in every year, with Rs 0 recorded, while the next-lowest total is Rs 99.78 lakh for Govindapur. Because sanctioned amounts are available for only about one in six activities, this does not establish that Chikilli received no approvals; urgently check for missing, unmatched or unentered sanction records.
===FINDING 14===
LEAD: Rs 1.02 crore of voucher-linked General-category spending is classified under grant components labelled “Other,” rather than tied or untied.
DETAIL: “Other” is the smallest component group in every year from 2020-21 to 2025-26 and represents 3.6% of the Rs 28.48 crore recorded total. Identify the components included in this category and confirm that the classification is valid and consistent across years.
===FINDING 15===
LEAD: The smallest and largest GP population groups consistently have the lowest aggregate sanctioned amounts in the sample.
DETAIL: GPs with under 2,500 people account for Rs 2.73 crore, or 9.5% of recorded sanctions, while those with 10,000 people and above account for Rs 4.82 crore, or 16.7%; the two middle-size groups each account for more than Rs 10 crore. These are aggregate totals and sanction records exist for only about one in six activities, so they do not establish unequal access; compare record coverage and sanctions per GP and per person before deciding whether follow-up is needed.

===FINDING 4===
LEAD: The recorded gap between expenditure and planned cost is largest in Kalimela and Bheden, averaging Rs 5.90 crore and Rs 5.60 crore below plan per Gram Panchayat. These blocks should be prioritised for reconciliation of plans, expenditure and unfinished works.
DETAIL: Across the 16 sampled blocks, the corresponding gaps were much smaller in Bhubaneswar and Lahunipara, at Rs 87.50 lakh and Rs 90.62 lakh below plan per GP. Gaps were broadly distributed across blocks for Mixed and SC-majority GPs, while the ST-majority group showed no clear pattern. Several block averages are based on only one GP, so the next review should check the underlying records rather than treat this as a block-wide conclusion.

===FINDING 13===
LEAD: Sharagada and Dutimendi show the largest GP-level gaps between recorded expenditure and sanctions, at Rs 85.77 lakh and Rs 57.38 lakh below sanction respectively. Chikilli records no gap.
DETAIL: The other GPs closest to sanction include Govindapur, Hirlipali, Barimunda and Bhatigaon, with gaps ranging from Rs 6.94 lakh to Rs 10.81 lakh. The gaps were broadly distributed among Mixed and SC-majority GPs, but there was no clear pattern for ST-majority GPs. Officials should reconcile sanctions, expenditure and work status in Sharagada and Dutimendi and confirm whether Chikilli’s zero variance is supported by complete records.

===FINDING 19===
LEAD: Mixed-composition GPs lead on 57 of 74 indicators, but they also represent 15 of the 20 sampled GPs and 76.0% of the 12,704 activities. The pattern should therefore be treated mainly as a scale signal, not evidence of stronger performance.
DETAIL: Important exceptions include completed works and average household tap-water coverage, where ST-majority GPs lead, and average plan variance, where SC-majority GPs lead. Photo evidence also looks different on a per-GP basis: ST-majority GPs averaged 488.5 uploads, Mixed GPs 441.1 and SC-majority GPs 224.3, based on only 2, 15 and 3 GPs respectively. Reviews should compare per-GP or population-adjusted figures and inspect the small ST- and SC-majority groups before drawing conclusions by social composition.

===FINDING 23===
LEAD: Recorded expenditure across the nine sampled districts was Rs 51.96 crore below planned cost, with Ganjam accounting for the largest district gap at Rs 17.85 crore and Bargarh next at Rs 9.72 crore. These two districts warrant first attention in plan-to-expenditure reconciliation.
DETAIL: Ganjam and Bargarh also account for 21.4% and 24.1% of the 12,704 activities, so their larger totals may partly reflect their greater activity volumes; the data does not establish why the gaps occurred. Among the available per-GP comparisons, Bargarh averaged Rs 2.43 crore below plan, while Khordha averaged Rs 87.50 lakh below plan. The gap was broadly spread across districts for Mixed and SC-majority GPs, with no clear pattern for ST-majority GPs; review both district totals and GP-level records.

===FINDING 29===
LEAD: Among sampled GPs with a Panchayat Bhawan, Mixed-composition GPs account for the majority on 58 of 74 indicators and 81.1% of the 8,983 activities. This concentration should not be read as better performance without adjusting for the number and size of GPs.
DETAIL: SC-majority GPs lead on completed works, while ST-majority GPs lead on average household tap-water and toilet figures. Photo uploads per GP were also higher for the ST-majority category—424.0, compared with 216.1 for Mixed and 209.0 for SC-majority—but that ST figure comes from only one GP. At review, compare per-GP service, completion and evidence measures and examine the single ST-majority GP before generalising.

===FINDING 31===
LEAD: Mixed-composition GPs with a Panchayat Bhawan record the highest values on 61 of 74 indicators, but they also account for 81.1% of activities in this subset. Several operational indicators do not follow that pattern and merit separate review.
DETAIL: SC-majority GPs lead on completed works, while ST-majority GPs lead on average photo uploads, household tap-water and toilets, and the average plan variance. The ST-majority photo average was 424.0 uploads per GP, against 216.1 for Mixed and 209.0 for SC-majority, but it represents only one GP; the Mixed and SC figures represent 11 and 2 GPs. Officials should review these exceptions at GP level and avoid treating social composition as an explanation.

===FINDING 33===
LEAD: Mixed-composition GPs account for the majority on 53 of 74 indicators, alongside 76.0% of all 12,704 activities in the sample. The aggregate dominance largely reflects where the sample’s activity volume sits and is not, by itself, a performance finding.
DETAIL: ST-majority GPs are the exception for completed works, while several per-GP financial and approval measures show either different or no clear patterns.
